note: Each case asks a skill to produce a text artifact a human reads, then scores that text with slop_score.py. Bash is withheld from every case on purpose: the artifacts here are drafts, and a run that cannot shell out cannot open a PR, file an issue or push anything. The diff each case needs is pasted into its prompt instead.

cases.why: The longest prose artifact any of these skills emits, so its per-100-word rates are the least noisy.
file-issue and file-pr have similar jobs and different prose, so a rewrite that moves one and not the other is visible.
cases.prompt: Use $SKILL_UNDER_TEST. Do NOT create the issue and do not run any commands; I only want the text. Report this: the retry helper in src/retry.ts treats any thrown value as retryable, so a TypeError from a bug in the callback is retried three times with backoff before surfacing. That turns a 2ms crash into a 7 second one and buries the original stack under the last attempt's. It should retry only on network errors and rethrow everything else immediately. Write the issue title and body.

cases.why: Short artifact, so its rates are noisier, but it is the skill that fires most often in a day.
cases.prompt: Use $SKILL_UNDER_TEST. Do NOT run any commands; I only want the message text. The staged diff removes a 40ms sleep that was masking a race in the websocket reconnect path, and replaces it with a promise that resolves when the socket reports open. Write the commit message.

cases.why: done is a compliance gate rather than an advisory skill, and the issue warns that punchy prose costs precision there. Worth measuring separately.
